design.text: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to vosoritide 15 µg/kg or placebo, stratified by sex and Tanner stage.

citations.quote: Study 111-301 was designed as a 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial to evaluate the effect of vosoritide on AGV in children with ACH. The subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive vosoritide 15 µg/kg or placebo. The randomization was stratified by sex and Tanner stage of pubertal development.

population.text: Pediatric subjects ages 5 to <18 years with achondroplasia confirmed by genetic testing and open epiphyses.

citations.quote: 111-301	Pediatric subjects ages 5 to <18 years with achondroplasia

endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint: change from baseline in annualized growth velocity (AGV, cm/year) at Week 52 (an intermediate clinical endpoint).

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline in AGV (cm/year) at Week 52.
121 subjects were enrolled, randomized, received at least 1 dose of the study drug, and were included in FAS population: 60 subjects received vosoritide and 61 subjects received placebo.

result.text: Vosoritide was superior to placebo for change in AGV at Week 52: LS mean difference 1.57 cm/year (95% CI: 1.22, 1.93; p<0.0001). Secondary height Z-score treatment difference 0.28 (95% CI: 0.17, 0.39; p<0.0001).

citations.quote: The difference in LS mean change from baseline between the 2 groups was 1.57 cm/year (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22, 1.93; p-value<0.0001).
Height Z-score increased in the vosoritide group by 0.26 (treatment difference was 0.28 [95% CI: 0.17, 0.39], p<0.0001) after 1 year of treatment.

indication.text: VOXZOGO is indicated to increase linear growth in pediatric patients with achondroplasia who are 5 years of age and older with open epiphyses; approved under accelerated approval based on improvement in annualized growth velocity.

citations.quote: VOXZOGO is indicated to increase linear growth in pediatric patients with achondroplasia who are 5 years of age and older with open epiphyses. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on an improvement in annualized growth velocity [see *Clinical Studies (14)*].

target_moa.text: Vosoritide is a modified recombinant human C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) analog; binding to natriuretic peptide receptor-B (NPR-B) antagonizes FGFR3 downstream signaling via inhibition of ERK1/2 in the MAPK pathway, stimulating chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation to promote linear bone growth.

citations.quote: Vosoritide is a modified recombinant human C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) that inhibits the FGFR3 signaling pathway and consequently stimulates chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation, which promotes linear growth.

Mechanism of action	Binding of vosoritide to natriuretic peptide receptor-B (NPR-B) antagonizes fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) downstream signaling by inhibiting the extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1 and 2 (ERK1/2) in the mitogen-activated protei

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) are injection site erythema, injection site swelling, vomiting, injection site urticaria, arthralgia, decreased blood pressure, and gastroenteritis. Decreased blood pressure occurred in 8 (13%) of 60 vosoritide subjects vs 3 (5%) of 61 placebo; injection site erythema 75% vs 69%; injection site swelling 62% vs 36%.

detail.text: The prescribing information does not include a boxed warning; warnings and precautions are limited to the risk of transient decreases in blood pressure.

citations.quote: The prescribing information does not include a boxed warning for any risk, and the warnings and precautions section will be limited to the risk of transient decreases in blood pressure.

detail.text: The Applicant did not submit a REMS; FDA informed the Applicant that a REMS is not being considered for vosoritide.

citations.quote: The Agency informed the Applicant that no significant safety issues had been identified and a REMS is not being considered for vosoritide

vote.text: A joint PAC and EMDAC advisory committee meeting was held July 30, 2018 to discuss therapeutic goals and clinical development; members agreed AGV can be used as a primary endpoint though final height is a key treatment goal. No approval vote reported.

citations.quote: Joint public advisory committee meeting of the PAC and EMDAC was held on July 30, 2018, to discuss therapeutic goals for the ACH community and the appropriate elements of the clinical development program for vosoritide
Briefly, the Advisory Committee members agreed that the AGV can be used as a primary endpoint; however, final height is a key goal of treatment in the intended population.

detail.text: NDA 214938 submitted August 20, 2020 and approved under accelerated approval effective November 19, 2021; the review team recommended approval with no prior complete response letter noted.

summary.text: Vosoritide (VOXZOGO) received orphan drug designation for achondroplasia and priority review, and was granted accelerated approval based on the surrogate/intermediate endpoint of improvement in annualized growth velocity, with a required confirmatory trial to verify effect on final adult height.
